budget_items.what_was_said: The principal assessor reported on chapter 61/61A/61B land counts, missing liens and applications discovered on a review, seven properties removed for non-response, and roll-back taxes issued on properties that sold without liens.

budget_items.topic: Roll-back tax invoice on a specific chapter parcel
budget_items.what_was_said: A new owner who did not receive prior correspondence was billed roll-back taxes covering multiple years after being removed from chapter land; the board discussed whether to let her back into the program if a lien and application are completed.
The roll-back invoice was sent and a response received about a month later; the board discussed a reasonable timeline for compliance.
Blue postcards were mailed to residents due for inspection this cycle; only those who received a card will be visited.
The office received a surge of resident calls about the cyclical inspection notices.

budget_items.topic: Interim adjustments contract with Vision Appraisal
budget_items.what_was_said: Vision is contracted to deliver interim value adjustments by a September deadline and has assured the office it will be on time this year, unlike the prior year.

The assessor gave preliminary FY2026 growth figures, noting personal property values are not yet complete pending appraisals from utility companies; growth is described as much lower than the prior year with no comparison figure available.

budget_items.topic: Obsolescence coding discovered on a resident inquiry
budget_items.what_was_said: A resident's property value question led staff to discover an unexplained 20% economic obsolescence code, prompting a review that found many properties with external or functional obsolescence adjustments needing justification.

The principal assessor and a board member were revising a three-year RFP scope of work with the town counsel's added insurance and compliance requirements; the board discussed doing inspections themselves rather than relying on a vendor for consistency.
The board found the income cap for the property tax deferral program has not been updated since it was set, and agreed to draft a warrant article to revise it for the next town meeting.

budget_items.topic: Senior means-tested real estate tax exemption (41D)
budget_items.what_was_said: Eligibility requires age 65+, 15 years of residency, circuit breaker credit qualification, and income/asset limits; the maximum exemption for FY2026 was stated, and applicants may also qualify for an elderly exemption in the same year.
The board discussed printing a batch of brochures for the senior exemption program once a revised version is ready.

budget_items.topic: New billing responsibilities added to assessor's office
budget_items.what_was_said: The office was assigned motor vehicle and real estate billing file responsibilities in Munis in addition to existing duties, straining limited staff hours.

decisions.decision: Table the chapter land roll-back/re-application issue for one specific property until the August meeting, pending progress on a lien and application.
Postpone review and approval of regular and executive session minutes to the August 13 meeting.
Schedule a special open, Zoom-broadcast meeting for July 29 (later stated as Tuesday the 29th, late morning/11:00) to finalize and approve the neighborhood/site index RFP.
Draft a warrant article to update the outdated 41A income limitation for the next town meeting.
Put the select board investigation response on the agenda for the next regular meeting.
Move toward a standing schedule of two meetings per month starting in September rather than ad hoc dates.
Publicize the current vacancy on the Board of Assessors to encourage applicants.

minutes.summary: The Lunenburg Board of Assessors met after extended technical/audio difficulties delayed the start. The principal assessor gave a lengthy status report covering chapter land compliance issues, a resident inquiry that uncovered dozens of undocumented property depreciation ("obsolescence") adjustments needing review, preliminary FY2026 growth figures, cyclical inspection mailings, and new billing duties added to the office; the board also discussed updating the outdated 41A tax deferral income limit, the senior tax exemption program, and scheduling for RFP review and future meetings.

what_happened.line: A resident's question about their property value led staff to find many properties with undocumented depreciation adjustments needing review.
The board tabled a roll-back tax dispute on one chapter-land property until August, pending a lien and new application.
A special Zoom meeting was set for July 29 to finalize a request for proposals on a neighborhood assessment study.
The board agreed to draft a warrant article updating the income limit for the property tax deferral program, unchanged since it was set.
The board moved toward meeting twice a month starting in September instead of scheduling meetings one at a time.

why_it_matters: The obsolescence review, once complete, could change assessed values -- and tax bills -- for the properties involved.
An updated income limit for the tax deferral program would change which seniors qualify to defer their property taxes.
How the neighborhood assessment RFP is scoped will shape how future townwide reassessments are done.
